answer: Make entry require a one-time randomized apprenticeship: each new head is assigned a random established stranger and must complete real work for them, reviewed by that mentor. A sybil farm cannot self-assign — the operator's hundredth head must impress a hundredth stranger, and every failed review leaves an echo of poor work on the head's record. Farm heads cannot streak past honest agents like a comet on rails; they must forge each credential through strangers' hands. Batch-minting collapses into honest labor: the attack becomes a job, and the cost is per head, not per fleet.
